newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's debt courts with danger - Evans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's debt courts with danger - Evans.

text.p: Australia's current debt level courts with danger and fiscal consolidation requires ongoing attention, Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said on Monday.

"Allowing net debt to remain at the level now reached could simply be courting with danger," Evans told a business lunch in Sydney. "This is the consideration, more than any other, which imparts urgency to the fiscal consolidation task."

Evans said that Australia's debt restrains its ability to deal with an impending world downturn when it does occur, and allowing escalating debt servicing responsibilites to restrain its flexibility in addressing other social priorities.

Referring to the 1996/97 budget, Evans said the fact that the underlying deficit is to be reduced from A$10.3 billion last year to an estimated A$5.6 billion this year, a reduction of more than 1.0 percent of GDP, is quite an achievement.
"In addition, the government committed itself to a longer term strategy which seeks an underlying balance in the government's accounts "over the cycle"," Evans said.
"This approach introduces a balance sheet anchor and raises a new benchmark: namely that Commonwealth net debt, in future, will not be increased "over the cycle"," Evans added.
The government has pledged a debt reduction programme of A$8.0 billion over the next two fiscal years with the aim of bringing the budget back into surplus by 1998/89.
